title: Evolith Rule Overrides
description: GT-678 — a tenant's per-rule delta over the Core corpus: disable, downgrade, de-block or harden ONE rule at a time, with a rationale, an approver and (for waivers) an expiry. Authored inside the satellite and referenced from its `evolith.yaml` (`spec.rulesets.overrides: <path relative to the satellite root>`). Read by `RulesetValidatorService.validate`, which every surface (CLI `validate`/`evaluate`, MCP `evolith-validate`/`evolith-evaluate`, REST `/architecture/validate-satellite` and `/evaluate`) traverses; validated against this schema before anything runs, and a document that fails it aborts the run with a named error (never ignored). Every override that changes a run is named in the result under `overrides.applied` (from → to, approver, expiry, source); every override that could not be honoured is named under `overrides.rejected` with a code. A blocking criterion can be WAIVED (time-boxed and approved) but never REMOVED: `enabled: false` or `blocking: false` on a `blocking: true` rule without both `approvedBy` and `expiresOn` is rejected as `OVR-BLOCKING-REMOVED` and fails the run closed.

tenantId.description: Opaque tenant identifier. Echoed for audit; the Core never resolves it (ADR-0101).

effectiveDate.description: ISO date from which the document applies (informational; the engine gates on `expiresOn`, not on this).

approvedBy.description: Who approved the DOCUMENT. Does not stand in for the per-override `approvedBy` a waiver of a blocking criterion requires.

rules.description: Keyed by Core rule id (e.g. `ACL-02`). An id the corpus does not carry is reported as `OVR-UNKNOWN-RULE`; nothing is loosened by a typo, so the run stays at least as strict as the corpus.

enabled.description: `false` removes the rule from evaluation; it is reported as disabled with its source. On a `blocking: true` rule this is a waiver and needs `approvedBy` + `expiresOn`.

severity.description: The severity the rule is evaluated and reported at. `SHOULD NOT` collapses to `SHOULD`, exactly as the corpus loader collapses it. Downgrading a `blocking: true` rule needs `approvedBy` (recorded); raising is always allowed.

blocking.description: `false` on a `blocking: true` rule is a waiver of a blocking criterion and needs `approvedBy` + `expiresOn`; `true` (hardening) is always allowed.

rationale.description: Why. Required on every override so an auditor never finds a softening without a reason.

approvedBy.description: Who approved THIS override. Required to waive a blocking criterion or to downgrade its severity.

expiresOn.description: Last day (inclusive, UTC) the override is in force. Past it the override is ignored and reported as `OVR-EXPIRED`. Required to waive a blocking criterion.
